text:
Emily W: Quick heads-up — I spun up the new llama3-7b-int8 build for onboarding and ran a regional benchmark across h100/us-east, a100/us-west, and h100/eu-west with the new edge routing policy enabled. Results look skewed at the tail after the routing flip.

Raj P: Can you paste the p50/p95 + throughput numbers?

Emily W: Sure — small summary from the 10k synthetic prompt run (batch=1, async KV cache warmup):
``` 
h100  | us-east (direct)    | p50=36ms  p95=120ms  thr=120 req/s/GPU
a100  | us-west (via edge)  | p50=42ms  p95=230ms  thr=95 req/s/GPU
h100  | eu-west (mixed)     | p50=55ms  p95=300ms  thr=80 req/s/GPU
```
Notes: all runs used int8 quantized weights, flash-attn enabled on H100 builds; A100 used triton kernel fallback.

Linh T: p95 jump on a100/us-west looks like routing + kernel combo. Did you run with prefix caching enabled on the edge proxy?

Emily W: Yes prefix caching on, but the edge-pop-failover we flipped routes ~25% of traffic through a proxy path that adds ~40-70ms of egress. That explains the p50 bump a bit, but p95 looks amplified — possibly due to cold-KV misses + triton kernel jitter.

Sam G: deploy-bot shows the routing change went out just before your run, right?

deploy-bot: Routing policy updated: edge-pop-failover=on for us-west at 2024-03-05T11:07:12Z (initiated by infra/rollout).

Raj P: Two quick checks: 1) repeat run with edge-pop-failover off; 2) run same config but force flash-attn/triton parity (if possible) to isolate kernel impact. If p95 drops with failover off then routing is the culprit.

Emily W: On it. I'll schedule a) direct-only rerun b) A/B forcing flash-attn on A100 (experimental shim) and c) increase warmup to 500 requests to amortize cold KV. Uploading logs and dashboards shortly: <https://app.redwood.dev/dashboards/bench/1719> :mag:

Linh T: Also capture GPU kernel churn and swap counters — last time that explained weird tails when we mixed kernels. Can you grab /metrics/kernel_switch and /metrics/kv_miss_rate for the same windows?

Emily W: Yup — included kernel_switch spikes in the dashboard. Preliminary observation: a100 shows 2x kernel-switch events coincident with the highest p95 latency windows.

Sam G: If routing is the main factor, we should adjust the failover policy to preserve latency-sensitive routes for small prompts and only failover long prompts that tolerate extra hops. Might be a quick config change rather than revert.

Emily W: Action items: 1) rerun direct-only (edge-pop-failover off) — ETA 20m; 2) rerun with extended warmup 500 — ETA 40m; 3) try forcing flash-attn shim on A100 (experimental) — ETA EOD. Will post updated p50/p95.

Raj P: Perfect. If the p95 persists after routing off + warmup, we'll open an infra ticket to dig into triton kernel tail behavior.

Sam G: FYI for capacity sizing: these numbers imply we should provision ~18% more concurrency on a100 pools in us-west if failover remains. Let's wait for reruns before changing commits. :clipboard:
